sources.title: Tilman Nagel: Buyids
sources.note: Main history, family principalities and ending. Entry typo 545/1062 not repeated; Fars ending compressed as early 1060s since exact sequence differs from other scholarship.

sources.title: Bürgel and Mottahedeh: Adud al-Dawla
sources.note: Direct scholarly article, Arabic learning/library paragraphs and building/festival paragraphs. Contemporary Muqaddasi and Biruni accounts explicitly attributed in public text.

sources.title: Judith A. Lerner: Band-e Amir in Iran
sources.note: Contemporary accounts, physical construction and later repairs. Erroneous calendar equivalence 356/975 avoided; only tenth century. Irrigation counts are medieval reports, not modern measurements.

sources.title: Ashmolean Museum: Buyid silver dirham HCR14387
sources.note: Direct object catalogue, Arabic reverse field and English translation; Fasā,348 AH/959 to 960,2.91 g,25.7 mm. Sample الامير العدل exactly from reverse, translated the Just Amir.

sources.title: D. M. Dunlop: Ibn Marzuban, Buyid hospital administrator
sources.note: Full scholarly biography;982 foundation, religious-law/sciences education, hospital superintendence and uncertainty over clinical role.

sources.title: US National Library of Medicine: al-Majusi’s Complete Book of the Medical Art
sources.note: Institutional manuscript catalogue: patron Adud, organization/anatomy/surgery, MS A 26.1 copied 1208. Do not assign surviving later copy to Buyid period.

sources.title: Paul Kunitzsch: Abd al-Rahman al-Sufi
sources.note: Scholarly biography, Buyid patronage, own observations and coordinates epoch 1 October 964, illustrated classical/Arabic constellation traditions. Avoid disputed 1009 Bodleian manuscript dating.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Shiites of Iraq
sources.note: Buyid patronage, Baghdad Karkh scholars, Sabur library 991 to 992, Abbasid suzerainty and communal tensions. No universal religious identity inferred.

sources.title: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art: gold ewer F1943.1
sources.note: Direct museum catalogue:966 to 977 object field versus patron reign 967 to 978; public date broad tenth century. Inscription apparently genuine, later handle, authenticity debate and reported provenance qualified.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: disputed Buyid silk, 30.67
sources.note: Current object date metadata directly checked. Earlier packet included related Abegg radiocarbon details; these were not freshly accessible and are not retained in this expanded public card.

sources.title: Wilferd Madelung: Deylamites
sources.note: Buyid brothers established Fars, Isfahan, Ray and Baghdad principalities; tenth-century origins and overthrow by 1062. Used for shared historical identity, not imported polygon validation.

sources.title: C. E. Bosworth: Divan, government office
sources.note: Buyid section: finance, correspondence and army departments, Abbasid administrative continuity. Same work as Saffarid runtime source; cumulative budget checked.

sources.title: Wilferd Madelung: Al-e Bavand
sources.note: Sayyeda paragraph: after Fakhr al-Dawla died in 997 she ruled Ray for her minor son Majd al-Dawla. Does not resolve disputed genealogy or inconsistent death date in another entry.

sources.title: David Whitehouse: Excavations at Siraf, Third Interim Report (1970)
sources.note: Original Iran 8 (1970), pages 1 to 18, read in the full journal reproduction https://www.scribd.com/doc/105587008/Iran-08-1970 (not its automated summary). House N description and discussion of decorated houses, streets, roof pipes and possible latrines. One underlying work budget.

sources.title: Robert Hillenbrand: Archaeology, Islamic Iran
sources.note: Siraf excavation synthesis: Indian Ocean trade, food and mountain water supplies, excavated houses and craft evidence. No unqualified town population estimate or inferred religious identity repeated.

sources.title: British Museum: Siraf Class BUFRAB cooking pots
sources.note: Original catalogue class listing includes cooking-pot 2007,6001.4038, ninth to tenth century, made in India and excavated at Siraf. Checked full indexed original listing; a subsequent direct fetch returned an internal error. No recipe or specific user inferred.

sources.title: Museum of Islamic Art, Doha: planispheric astrolabe SI.5.1999
sources.note: Tara Desjardins, Discover Islamic Art/Museum With No Frontiers: inscribed maker al-Khujandi and date AH 374 (984 to 985), 33 rete markers including six bird beaks. Ray or Baghdad production and possible Baghdad use remain qualified.

batchIdentityNotes.finding: New missing association to existing buyid-dynasty card. Buwayhid/Buyid are spellings of the same dynasty. The Iran/Iraq-centered world-1000 feature is broadly compatible with its principalities, but its repeated world-1200 feature is anachronistic. Retain imported 1000 to 1279 as map coverage only. Historical phases concern the tenth and eleventh centuries; shared public map paragraph preserves the different error in buyid-dynasty.

Existing canonical card expanded from 13 to 22 passages, retaining its historical phases and separate Afghanistan/Pakistan geometry warning. Existing override remains 1200 to 1279 map coverage. This replacement adds only one new indexed association, not two new civilization cards.
Excluded. The 1000 to 1100 feature lies in Sindh/Baluchistan (63.6 to 71.405 E, 23.675 to 32.532 N), so no confident association is made merely from a similar label.
